subject: Enterprise no-learn implementation & IP delivery plan

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orionhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: No-training commitment + prompt/response ownership — implementation asks

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile. Before Procurement moves this forward we need clarity on three operational items that must be contractually guaranteed:

1) No-training / no model improvement: we require a contractual "no-learning" commitment for PII and patient prompts; please confirm what operational controls you can provide and whether this is limited to a customer account flag or requires a private deployment.

2) Prompt/Response ownership: we need a plain-English statement that Orion retains exclusive rights to prompts and generated responses, and the ability to export the conversational logs on demand.

3) Subprocessors & evidence: please share your subprocessor inventory and say how Orion can get evidence (audit logs, SOC reports) that subprocessors did not access data for model training. Also clarify cross-border transfer protections — we prefer EU/US residency for hosted logs or the option for a dedicated instance on AWS in us-east-1.

Procurement timeline: we aim to have signed paper by 2026-11-18. Can Redwood provide a proposed SOW and DPA redline with operational attachments this week?

Regards,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Digital Platforms, Orion Health Systems
Liam.O'Connor@orionhealth.com

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Copying David (legal) and Jonas (infrastructure) so we can align on the operational evidence. High-level response and suggested next steps below: 

Quick answers:
- No-learning: we can offer a contractual no-training/no-model-improvement commitment for customer data. There are two standard delivery options: 1) Hosted account with "no-learn" toggle + detailed logging and evidence; 2) Private/Dedicated deployment (VPC or on-prem) where data never leaves your tenancy and training hooks are disabled by default.
- Prompt/Response ownership: Redwood will state that customers retain ownership of prompts and outputs. We also provide export endpoints and an SFTP export path for retention/archival.
- Subprocessors & evidence: attaching our current subprocessor inventory and a draft DPA redline. Jonas can produce a short audit package (SOC2 summary, access logs, and on-demand subprocessor access reports) for procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) I attach a draft SOW (Orion_No-Learn_SOW_v1.pdf) and our subprocessor CSV for your review.
2) David, can your team propose the minimal contract language for the no-learning pledge and ownership clause?
3) Jonas, can you confirm what evidence artifacts we can produce within 48 hours (audit logs, KMS residency attestation, subprocessor access timestamps)?
4) Liam/Procurement: is a 60-minute technical+legal call on Friday 11/7 workable?

We will also flag pricing impact — dedicated/private options add cost. Marissa will follow up on commercials.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Grace / David,

Thanks for the materials. A few clarifying points from legal that must appear in an acceptable redline: 

• Definition of "no-learning": we need a clear definition that covers (a) operator-side model updates that incorporate customer data, and (b) any offline research/benchmarking that could use derivative prompts/responses. We prefer language that prohibits both unless explicitly consented in writing.

• Prompt/Response IP: we require an explicit clause that grants Orion exclusive rights to customer-provided prompts and all outputs. Does Redwood require a limited license back for telemetry or model improvement? If so, it must be strictly scoped and opt-in.

• Retention and export: please confirm the maximum retention window for logs in hosted mode and provide the export SLA (time-to-export for full dataset).

• Subprocessor attestations: we will accept SOC2 + subprocessor access logs as primary evidence. Provide a sample log extract showing timestamps and actor IDs for at least one prior request. Also confirm whether access to data for operational reasons (debugging) can be done within an isolated environment and whether such access is logged and audited.

We will review the SOW but need these items in the DPA and SOW before we circulate to our InfoSec. Also note pricing approval will be contingent on the deployment model and export SLA.

Thanks — please respond before the proposed Friday call so we can prepare detailed questions.

— Priya Das
Senior Counsel, Orion Health Systems
From: david_kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Das <priya.das@orionhealth.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: No-training commitment + prompt/response ownership — implementation asks

Priya / Liam / Grace —

Thanks for the detail. Below are proposed redline-ready bullets we can include in the DPA and SOW. These are intentionally prescriptive to speed review: 

1) No-Learning / No-Model-Improvement: "Redwood agrees that data submitted by Customer (including prompts and generated responses) will not be used to train, fine-tune, evaluate, improve, or update Redwood models or any third-party models without the Customer's prior written consent. Operationally, Redwood will disable model-improvement pipelines for Orion's tenant and document that state in the controls section of the SOW."

2) Prompt & Output Ownership: "Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Data, including prompts and generated outputs. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual export right and will provide programmatic export and one-time SFTP export within the export SLA below."

3) Export SLA & Retention: "Redwood will retain conversational logs in hosted mode for a maximum of 90 days by default; upon Customer request Redwood will generate and deliver a full export within 48 hours. For customers who require longer retention or residency commitments, Redwood will offer Dedicated/Private deployments with configurable retention policies."

4) Subprocessors & Evidence: "Redwood will provide (a) a current subprocessor inventory; (b) SOC2 Type II summary; and (c) upon request a redacted access log extract that shows time-stamped actor IDs and actions for specified requests. Any operational access for debugging will be recorded, time-limited, and subject to Customer notification for sensitive datasets."

5) Pricing / Commercials: "Dedicated/private deployment and onshore KMS options will incur additional fees. Marissa to propose a commercial estimate by EOD 11/06."

Jonas: operational question — can we produce a redacted access-log snippet for a prior customer event that demonstrates actor IDs and timestamps? Also can you confirm KMS residency options (us-east-1, eu-west-1) and whether we can bind keys to customer-managed KMS?

If these bullets look good, Grace / Marissa / Jonas and I can incorporate them into a redline that we circulate to Orion.

-David
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
